A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, retaining the central semialgebraic characterization and several matching proofs despite the changed title and emphasis. All 24 pages of v1 and 18 pages of v2, including appendices and figures, support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions, expressivity results, and proofs. Its main text and appendices contain no original empirical results.

after.justification: Section 6 and Figure 1 report original softmax-transformer classification experiments on five polynomial counting languages, including testing on longer strings. Appendix D documents the setup.

M1.justification: The basic frequency and multiplication gadgets are retained. However, v2 Appendix A.2 introduces parallel composition of uniform-attention transformers without increasing depth, replacing v1's sequential composition. Appendix B uses this construction for two-layer universality instead of v1's quadratic-score construction, obtaining a procedure directly realizable with softmax attention.

E1.justification: v1 studies counting languages theoretically without dataset evaluation. v2 adds synthetic binary-classification datasets for L_k = {w: |w|_b <= |w|_a^k}, for k = 1 through 5, with training and ordinary testing up to length 500 and generalization testing at lengths 501-1000.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical comparisons against baseline methods. v2 evaluates its softmax classifiers; C-RASP, LTL with Counting, and polynomial separators are theoretical comparisons, not experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an experimental protocol absent from v1: 500,000 training examples, equally sized validation data, single-epoch training with validation-based selection, a grid over 1-5 layers and 1/2/4 heads, and evaluation using BCEWithLogitsLoss and accuracy on ordinary and longer-string test sets.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused length-generalization analysis comparing testing up to length 500 with testing at lengths 501-1000 across the five languages. v1 has no corresponding analysis. The architecture grid serves model selection and is not reported as an ablation or sensitivity study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. v2's single-epoch budget and selection of the best validation model do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 1 adds validation, test, and generalization losses plus classification accuracies for all five languages. Reported ordinary-test accuracy is 0.99 throughout; longer-string accuracies are 0.95, 0.94, 0.96, 0.97, and 0.96. These are new results, with no corresponding v1 measurements.

T1.justification: v2 adds the degree-versus-depth result SemiAlg[<=l] subset NoPE-AHAT[<=l,U] and a depth-preserving composition lemma, strengthening two-layer universality and undecidability to uniform attention and SMAT. It removes v1's TC0 separation, counter-machine/HORS/Petri-net results, and end-marker-free theory. The semialgebraic characterization, PARITY proof, one-layer QFPA characterization, and LTL-counting proof remain, sometimes relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction shift from NoPE hard-attention expressivity and circuit separation toward nonlinear counting in softmax transformers, empirical trainability, and limitations of C-RASP's learnability characterization. The central semialgebraic claim remains, while the TC0-separation contribution disappears and the two-layer claims explicitly encompass uniform attention and SMAT.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes unbounded precision and distinguishes expressivity from trainability. v2 removes the precision discussion and interprets its experiments as supporting efficient learning and a gap in C-RASP/RASP-L, attributing generalization differences to limited experimental exploration. It also newly identifies one-layer SMAT emptiness decidability as unresolved.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix D supplies experimental implementation information absent from v1: PyTorch encoders without positional encoding, 32 input features, feedforward dimension 64, dropout 0.3, and AdamW with learning rate 0.0001 and weight decay 0.01. It also documents training and model-selection settings, although neither PDF supplies experimental code or dataset access.

R1.justification: v2 substantially repositions the work around C-RASP, RASP-L, length generalization, vector-space models, and polynomial kernels, adding works including Huang et al. (2025), Zhou et al. (2024), and Yang and Chiang (2024). Much of v1's circuit-complexity, automata, and verification positioning and associated references is removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v1's separate results summary is replaced by introductory theorem statements; definitions become an expanded framework section, proofs and applications are reorganized, and several retained proofs move to appendices. The title and author order also change.

P2.justification: v1's expressivity-hierarchy diagram is removed. v2 introduces a results table paired with a logarithmic loss line plot in Figure 1 and a colored parallel-composition schematic in Figure 2. The title block, author arrangement, heading typography, and running page headers are also reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the depth construction and makes the ordinary-softmax connection explicit, while Figure 1 provides initial training evidence. However, v1's explicit unbounded-precision caveat disappears, and v2's broad efficient-learnability/C-RASP claims rely on five finite-length tasks with incompletely specified sampling and no uncertainty reporting. The stronger construction and empirical relevance coexist with weaker qualification of practical claims, leaving the net effect on overall quality unclear.
